method: 8 evals (2 traps), run with the skill and without any skill on Claude Haiku in fresh agents that never saw the expectations; graded blind by a separate grader against expectations written before the runs. The graded comparison is from round 1 (skill v1.0.0). Rounds 2-4 (v1.1.0, v1.2.0) re-ran the full audits repeatedly on the same sites to measure consistency; those runs were checked against the round-1 expectations by hand, not re-graded blind.

by_eval.eval: 4 trap: audit a site it can't see

consistency.what: The same site audited by separate fresh agents. Total score out of 100.

v1.1.0.note: same grade every run; Tallyhouse spread 9 points, mostly one issue scored in two checks

known_issues_fixed_after_grading: v1.0: same-site scores varied by up to 5 points and crossed a grade boundary (fixed by checklist scoring, 1.1-1.2)
v1.0: confidence reported High on 3-4 pages (fixed: --pages caps confidence)
v1.0: the consultant's next step leaked into the shareable report (fixed in 1.1; in 1.2 score.json no longer stores it)
v1.0: missed mobile viewport, privacy notice, navigation, CTA consistency and unconfigured GA4 (added as checks in 1.1)
where_no_skill_matched: Refusing to audit an unseen site and refusing to invent traffic: the base model mostly handles these. The skill's gains are a reproducible score, evidence on every finding, and catching measurement gaps that only show in raw HTML.
limits: Two fixture sites and Haiku only. Report length runs about 1,100-1,300 words against a 1,000-word target.
